_notes: Roles (dev-guide Sections 7.11 and 7.26). A role owns the tactics of a bot: there is no team-wide slider over them any more, so what a role says is what a bot does. `rangePref` names all three bands, best first, and `weaponPref` names archetypes, best first. A player builds a team by choosing a role for each of the three bots, which makes the composition one categorical choice that a batch can sweep. Every number is a placeholder. TBD Section 7.48.7: the Overwatch `weaponPref` holds the two archetypes that perform at range and nothing else: marksman fires 72.6 % of its shots long and precision 51.8 %. Every other archetype is under 17 %, so listing one would hand it a bonus over the rest for no measured reason -- splash is the highest peak DPS in the game at 63.7 and fires half its shots CLOSE, so a third place for it sends an Overwatch bot to fetch a close-range weapon. `denial` used to sit third at weight 1.36, nearly matching precision, and it fires 0.5 % of its shots long -- it is a close-range weapon. `versatile` sat fourth and `archetypeOf` can never return it, so that slot was dead and it diluted the two archetypes that do the work. Section 7.49: `tank` and `skirmisher` are measured the same way. Membership is the share of its shots an archetype fires in the role's preferred band, which breaks cleanly: long holds marksman 72.6 % and precision 51.8 % and then drops to 16.3 %; close holds denial 52.4, splash 50.3, heavy 49.2 and assault 48.5 and then drops to 20.0; mid holds denial 47.1, heavy 45.5, assault 43.5 and precision 39.7 and then drops to 33.8. Order inside a list is `weaponWorth` for that role, read with the preference emptied so the ranking cannot feed itself. `denial` is reserved to the tank: `hazardAvoidBelowTolerance` is 0.5, so a tank at 0.7 is the only role that will path through a hazard, and a denial weapon lays them. The dead `versatile` entry is gone from all three. Section 7.49.2: the band share decides the ORDER and it is not a filter. Truncating a list to its measured members made the roles worse, because `weaponWeight` gives an unlisted archetype 1.00, the floor of its scale, so a short list cannot say 'I do not want these' -- it says 'I am indifferent'. That lowers what an unknown weapon point is worth and keeps the bot on the starting rifle: measured on openfield, the baseline share of every shot runs 40.5 % at a list of two, 39.8 at three, 39.5 at four and 39.7 at five, and the role's win rate rises 53.0, 53.5, 54.3, 55.0 across the same four. So every archetype a role can use is listed, ordered by `weaponWorth`, and the order alone carries the identity: splash is 1.60 to a tank and 1.24 to an overwatch, marksman 1.60 to an overwatch and 1.10 to a tank.
